bone.note: Light-theme page ground; in dark it becomes the foreground and the counterpart of .band--ink.

bone-sunk.note: The one tonal step in the system: .band--sunk in light. Not a card, a recessed band.

ink.note: Dark-theme page ground, the entrance panel, and the light-theme .band--ink field.

drench-blue.note: The drench. Background only: as text on the dark ground it measures 2.9:1. Text that wants blue uses --link instead.

drench-blue-dark.note: The same drench lifted for the ink ground; both --blue and --drench take this value under [data-theme=dark].

acid.note: Means live and nothing else in content (.dot on the current role, .row-live on open-ended projects). Elsewhere only as the counter-colour inside a drenched or ink field. 1.00:1 on bone — never text on a light ground.

muted-light.note: --fg-2 in light: running secondary prose, leads, summaries.

faint-light.note: --fg-3 in light: labels, index numbers, org names, scrollbar thumb.

rule-light.note: Structural hairlines: between work rows, timeline entries, above the footer. Non-interactive, so no 3:1 requirement.

edge-light.note: Borders on interactive, self-contained controls — buttons, chips, filters, header pills. Measured 3.67:1 against bone.

on-drench-dark.note: Text riding on the drenched field in dark; light uses plain bone. Row org/summary derive from it via color-mix at 78% / 85%.

hero.purpose: The name only, edge to edge and uppercase, plus its ghosted repeat at the contact close. Sizes itself from --hero-ch, computed in Home.tsx from the longest line of the name, so a longer name shrinks instead of being clipped.

display-1.purpose: The statement in the ink band, the contact headline, project page titles. The only level where the .em italic word appears.

display-3.purpose: Skills-group titles, project pagination targets, empty-state headline.

emphasis.purpose: Bodoni Moda italic, exactly one word inside a Display 1 headline. Used twice on the whole site; that restraint is the rule.

lead.purpose: The sentence directly under a display headline. 34ch by default, 38ch in the hero, 44ch on a project page.

body.purpose: Running prose in project blocks and timeline summaries, capped at --measure (62ch).

small.purpose: Buttons, filters, nav labels, row summaries, footer. Weight 600.

label.purpose: Every metadata line — role and location under the name, block headings on project pages, dates, the entrance panel's bottom row. Uppercase, tracked 0.14em, in --fg-3.

fonts.note: Variable grotesque. Display type pins font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 100.
Not preloaded on purpose: a handful of glyphs, below the fold.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system has no elevation vocabulary. Nothing is lifted, nothing floats. Depth is ground-against-ground, hairlines, and stacking order alone.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Not elevation. A halo of the current background painted behind the focus outline so the ring stays visible when it lands on a drenched or ink field. On .band--drench and .band--ink it becomes color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 55%, transparent) with an acid outline.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default easing — heavy front-load, long settle. Colour changes, transforms, the text roll.

motion.name: ease-io
motion.purpose: Symmetrical in-out, for anything that wipes: the button fill, the row drench, the entrance exit.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover colour and border changes on pills and controls.

motion.name: row-drench
motion.purpose: The work row's 100vw field scales from scaleY(0), origin top on entry and bottom on exit, so the drench reads as directional rather than as a fade.

motion.name: wipe
motion.purpose: The button's ::before panel rising from translateY(101%).

motion.name: marquee-slide
motion.purpose: Seamless because the item list is duplicated and the track rendered twice. Pauses on hover via animation-play-state.

motion.name: enter-exit
motion.value: 1150ms var(--ease-io) forwards; holds to 74%, then translateY(-101%)
motion.purpose: The entrance panel's exit. A CSS animation on purpose: requestAnimationFrame is throttled in background tabs and low-power modes, and an overlay whose only way out is a JS frame can sit over the page indefinitely. JavaScript owns the digits and nothing else.

motion.name: theme-swap
motion.purpose: The body's crossfade when the theme selector flips.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global off-switch, plus per-component branches: the entrance is skipped entirely (display: none, animation: none), the marquee track and badge ring stop, and smooth scrolling reverts to auto.

breakpoints.purpose: Work row drops its index number; summary moves to column 1.
Timeline entries and project prose blocks collapse to one column.
Hero under-block and section heads collapse to one column, top-aligned.
Header nav becomes its own scrollable row inside the fixed bar; project page main/aside collapses.
Work row goes three-column; the summary moves under the title and clamps to two lines.

layoutTokens.name: --header-h
layoutTokens.purpose: Published by Header.tsx via ResizeObserver on the fixed header's offsetHeight. The hero and project pages reserve exactly this, because the notice bar's height changes with wrapping and language. Also drives scroll-padding-top.

layoutTokens.name: --hero-ch
layoutTokens.purpose: Computed in Home.tsx as Math.max(first.length, last.length, 5) and fed to --d-hero, so a longer name shrinks instead of overflowing.

layoutTokens.name: inner-max
layoutTokens.purpose: .band > .inner. Colour goes on the band so the field runs full-viewport while type stays measured.

contrast.floor: 4.5:1 for every text pair in both themes; lowest measured 4.64:1.
knownFailuresDesignedAround: --drench as text on the dark ground: 2.9:1 — which is why --link exists (blue on bone, acid on ink).
--acid on bone: 1.00:1 — which is why --focus is a separate role (ink on bone, acid on ink).
contrast.obligation: Changing --blue or --acid requires re-verifying every text pair in both themes.

narrative.overview:
This is a poster you can scroll. The name is set edge to edge at the scale it would have on a wall, and the page is built from full-width horizontal bands that each take a whole colour — never a neutral page with accents sprinkled over it. There are no cards, no shadows, no floating containers and no boxed layouts. Depth is made from grounds against each other and from hairline rules, nothing else. Where the reference sites use photography to carry the visual weight, this system uses colour arriving at page scale and type set larger than seems reasonable.

The build ships no imagery at all and there is no image generation available for it. That is the governing constraint, not a temporary gap: the creative load rests entirely on typography, colour fields, motion and layout. Two slots (.row-thumb in the work index, .proj-media on the project page) are wired to project.cover and stay inert until real screenshots arrive; adding one must not change the world around it.

This design replaces a first build that executed the developer-portfolio category standard and was rejected outright by the user ("On y est pas du tout", "beaucoup trop générique"). The rejected system — a neutral page, a hairline index, one small accent colour — is the confirmed anti-reference. Four sites were pinned in its place (gusta.studio, dineshrevunuru.com, huuuuue.agency, ryanritzenthaler.com), and their shared mechanism binds future work: display type as the primary content at absurd scale, two typefaces inside one headline, full-bleed colour fields, a marquee band, a rotating badge, and media treated as an object rather than a card.
keyCharacteristics: Display type at poster scale, edge to edge, uppercase for the name
Full-bleed colour fields that own entire sections and entire index rows
Bone over ink, or ink over bone — the same world inverted, both authored by hand
Exactly one didone italic word per headline, never two
Zero shadows, zero cards, zero intermediate corner radii
Every motion has a complete prefers-reduced-motion off-switch

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: Colour arrives as a field that owns a whole band or a whole row, edge to edge across the viewport. --drench is never an accent, never a border, never a small fill, never a hover tint on a corner. The work row proves the rule: its ::before is 100vw wide with a -50vw offset so the band escapes the container and runs the real width of the page.

rules.name: The Acid Means Live Rule
rules.body: --acid has exactly one semantic in content: this is currently running. A live role, an open-ended project. Anything else that wants attention uses --link or the drench. Using acid as a decorative highlight destroys the only signal in the system that carries meaning by colour alone.

rules.name: The Background-Only Rule
rules.body: --drench is a background. Text never takes it. Three separate roles exist because the same value cannot do all three jobs: --drench (field), --link (text — blue on bone, acid on ink), --focus (ring — ink on bone, acid on ink, because acid on bone is 1.00:1). Do not collapse them.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are the same world with the grounds swapped, both written by hand — dark is not a filter over light. .band--ink therefore inverts in dark (bone ground, ink text) so that a field stays a field instead of collapsing into the page ground it would otherwise match.

rules.name: The 4.5 Floor
rules.body: Every text pair in both themes clears 4.5:1, the lowest measuring 4.64:1. Interactive borders use --edge at 3.67:1 light and 3.43:1 dark. Anyone who changes --blue or --acid re-verifies every pair in both themes before shipping — those two values are load-bearing for the whole contrast budget.

rules.name: The One Italic Word Rule
rules.body: The .em span is exactly one word per headline. Not a phrase, not two words, not a whole clause. The build uses it twice on the whole site — "produits entiers" and "Travaillons ensemble" — and that restraint is the rule. A second .em inside the same headline is a defect, not a variation.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Three faces, one job each: Bricolage displays, Hanken reads, Bodoni emphasises. No face takes a second job, and there is no fourth face. Labels and metadata are Hanken tracked out, never a mono or a condensed cut.

rules.name: The Name Sizes Itself Rule
rules.body: --hero-ch is computed in Home.tsx from the longest line of the name (Math.max(first.length, last.length, 5)) and feeds --d-hero, which takes the smallest of 17.6vw, 17rem, and the width that actually fits between the gutters. A longer name shrinks; it is never clipped by overflow-x: hidden. Never hardcode a hero font-size, and never remove the inline --hero-ch.

rules.name: The Tight-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Display type is negatively tracked and its line-height sits below 1 (0.8 at hero, 0.88 at Display 1). Label type is the opposite: positively tracked at 0.14em and uppercase. There is no neutral middle — type is either packed or spaced out.

rules.name: The Measured Header Rule
rules.body: The header is fixed and measures itself: a ResizeObserver in Header.tsx publishes el.offsetHeight as --header-h on <html> (falling back to a resize listener, with a 5.5rem first-paint default in :root). The hero and the project page reserve exactly calc(var(--header-h) + …), and scroll-padding-top uses it too. This exists because the placeholder notice bar's height changes with text wrapping and language. Never hardcode a top offset; always spend --header-h.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: A new section is a .band with an .inner. If it takes colour it takes .band--drench, .band--sunk or .band--ink on the band element. A section that needs its own background but sits inside another band is a mistake — nest a .band inside a plain coloured wrapper instead, the way the ink band wraps the marquee and the statement.

rules.name: The Nothing-Disappears Rule
rules.body: Narrow viewports rearrange; they do not hide. Below 900px the header nav becomes its own horizontally-scrollable row inside the fixed bar rather than folding into a menu, so no section is unreachable. Below 1000px the row summary moves under the title and line-clamps rather than vanishing. A responsive rule that deletes content is a bug.

rules.name: The No-Card Rule
rules.body: Nothing is a card. Content is never wrapped in a bordered, radiused, shadowed, background-filled box to group it. Grouping is done by hairline, by band colour, or by grid position. A project entry is a row on a rule, not a tile; a project image is an object in the flow, not a thumbnail in a frame.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 999px or 0. There is no 4px, no 8px, no 12px. If a new element needs a corner, decide whether it is an interactive control (pill) or a structural surface (square) — there is no third answer.

rules.name: The One Icon System Rule
rules.body: Icons are drawn in a 16px box, 1.6 stroke, round caps and joins, currentColor, from the shared base spread in components/icons.tsx. No icon font, no icon package, no glyph characters, no mixed stroke weights. A new icon is added to that file with the same base.

rules.name: The CSS Owns the Exit Rule
rules.body: Anything that covers the page exits by CSS animation. JavaScript may drive the contents — the entrance panel's digits — but must never be the only way out: requestAnimationFrame is throttled in background tabs and low-power modes, and this shipped once as a panel that sat over the page indefinitely. The overlay is also decided before first paint, so it is present from the first frame or never, and it never locks scroll or gates content.

rules.name: The Contiguous Block Rule
rules.body: Two cascade bugs shipped during this build, both the same shape: a later same-specificity rule silently overriding an earlier display declaration. Every rule that controls one element's display therefore lives in a single contiguous block — the .preloader rules are kept that way deliberately, default and armed state together. Do not scatter an element's display across the stylesheet.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Total Rule
rules.body: Every animation has a prefers-reduced-motion branch that turns it fully off, and an entrance-style overlay is skipped entirely rather than shortened. The global reset collapses durations, and the entrance, marquee and badge each carry their own explicit off-switch on top of it.

dos: Do put colour on a .band, at full viewport width, owning the whole section — the Field Rule.
Do reserve header space with calc(var(--header-h) + …) on any page that starts at the top of the viewport — the Measured Header Rule.
Do use exactly one .em word per headline, in Bodoni Moda italic — the One Italic Word Rule.
Do reach for --link when blue needs to be text, and --focus when it needs to be a ring; --drench is a background only.
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce branch that turns it fully off, and make an entrance-style overlay skip, not shorten.
Do let CSS own the exit of anything that covers the page. JavaScript may drive the contents; it must never be the only way out.
Do keep all rules that control one element's display in a single contiguous block, .preloader-style.
Do mirror every :hover state onto :focus-within / :focus-visible, as the work row does.
Do collapse a grid to one column at the width its own content breaks at, and move content rather than hiding it.
Do add new icons to components/icons.tsx on the shared 16px / 1.6-stroke base.
donts: Don't add a shadow. Not on hover, not on a "card", not as a glow. The only box-shadow in the system is the focus-ring halo.
Don't wrap content in a bordered, radiused, filled box to group it — the No-Card Rule.
Don't introduce a corner radius between 0 and 999px — the Two Radii Rule.
Don't use --acid for anything except live in content, or as the counter-colour inside a drenched/ink field. It is never text on bone (1.00:1).
Don't set --drench as a text colour (2.9:1 on the dark ground), and don't change --blue or --acid without re-verifying every text pair in both themes against the 4.5:1 floor.
Don't add a fourth typeface, and don't give an existing one a second job.
Don't hardcode a hero font-size or drop the inline --hero-ch; the name must be able to shrink instead of clipping.
Don't hide navigation or content at narrow widths — rearrange it.

Don't treat imagery as a thumbnail in a frame. .row-thumb and .proj-media are wired for real screenshots; an image arrives as an object in the flow, filling its slot with object-fit: cover and no border, radius or shadow.
Don't re-introduce the rejected category standard: a neutral page with a hairline index and a single small accent colour is the confirmed anti-reference for this project.
